name: Southeast Face / Leroy Basin
approach: From the Phelps Creek Trailhead (3,500 ft, at the end of the Phelps Creek spur off Chiwawa River Road/FR-62), follow Phelps Creek Trail #1511 south. The tread is in generally good maintained shape, with only occasional overgrown brush in late summer. At about 3.5 miles (roughly 1.5-2 hours in), the trail runs alongside Leroy Creek — a large waterfall visible up-valley from the switchbacks is a good landmark — where an unsigned but well-beaten climbers' path breaks off on the north (true right) side of the creek. This use trail is unmaintained but easy to follow from steady foot traffic; it climbs very steeply, gaining roughly 2,000 ft in about 1.5-1.9 miles while staying above Leroy Creek, which is the last reliable water before the basin. It eases into Leroy Creek Basin (~6,050-6,100 ft, about 5.4 mi and ~2,700 ft gain from the trailhead), a broad heather-and-boulder cirque that is the standard base camp, with good tent sites and running water. From camp most parties continue north/northeast across meadow and rock toward a col (~7,800 ft) on Seven Fingered Jack's south shoulder, roughly another hour. This whole upper section is cross-country with sparse cairns — Fernow itself isn't visible from most of Leroy Basin, and the peak has a well-earned reputation for tricky route-finding, so carry a map/GPS track rather than counting on a visible target. From the col, the route loses about 1,000 ft into the head of the Ice/Big Creek drainage, crossing beneath a shrinking glacier remnant (open crevasses have been reported here — rope up for the crossing or give it a wide berth), then curves west onto the broad talus/scree slopes on Fernow's south/southeast side and climbs roughly a mile toward the summit block, mostly class 2-3 talus with one notably exposed 'unexpected crux' — a sloped, gravel-covered slab with about a 30 m drop below and a 10 m traverse across it, rated only class 2 but consequential.
